approved_scope: Earlier CPU-visible prefill delivery through existing RunnerConfig token budget, retaining C attention/math/cache and fixed 8192-token prefill chunk
hypothesis: Because the runner executes prefill rows serially but Engine publishes only after the whole batch, an 8192-token runner budget should publish each completed 8K prompt's first token earlier. It does not remove model work or change decode batch width. Extra Engine steps may cost throughput, and prefill-first scheduling may increase early requests' first inter-token gap.

existing_api_limits: The scheduler selects prefills first and dispatches homogeneous phases; reducing the budget does not interleave ready decode rows.
Engine.step(phase=decode) filters the normal selected cohort rather than overriding prefill priority.
A synchronous runner cannot publish partial ForwardOutput rows through Engine.step before returning.
True prefill/decode interleaving would require a scheduler/core policy decision outside this approved lane; no such change made.
unresolved_coverage: GPU/full-checkpoint parity has not been rerun for the changed scheduling yet.
GPU TTFT, TPOT, full completion throughput, and per-request latency trade-off are unmeasured.
CPU publication step counts do not establish GPU timing or throughput.
No HTTP serving, asynchronous overlap, output-quality or new arrival-distribution claims.
